what_happened: The operator ran `athena correct` on job 20261024-220848-engm's reading and told it to time a synthetic fixture. The request still said to time this repository. The critic judged the corrected reading a misread of the request, so planning stopped. That cost one run ($0.88) and the operator had to re-ask.
cause: The correction path treats the request and the reading as separate things. It accepts any correction text without comparing it to the request. The request stays the source of truth for the critic, so a correction that changes scope or a requirement turns into a contradiction that only the critic catches, after the run is paid for.
prevention: When `athena correct` is run on a reading, check the correction text against the request. If it overrides an explicit requirement (for example the subject to measure), warn the operator and ask them to confirm. On confirmation, require an edited request or a new request instead of a reading correction. The check could be a cheap model comparison of the correction with the request, run before any planning run is paid for.
proposed_request: Make `athena correct` check a reading correction against the job's request before it accepts the correction. If the correction contradicts or drops an explicit requirement stated in the request (such as measuring this repository versus a synthetic fixture), it must refuse by default and tell the operator to edit the request or submit a new one. It may proceed only when the operator passes an explicit override flag, and the override must be recorded. Add tests with one correction that conflicts with the request and is refused, one that is consistent and accepted, and one conflicting correction that proceeds with the override flag and is recorded.
